chunks: And in the narration of Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

“The one in iʿtikāf in Makkah may perform salat (prayer) in whichever of its houses he wishes, while the one in iʿtikāf elsewhere does not perform salat (prayer) except in the mosque that he designated.”

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque in which the retreat is observed
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفُ: the person performing iʿtikāf, a spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.بُيُوتِهَا: its houses, referring to the houses of Makkah
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, which is given a distinct ruling here

ai.seo_question: Where may a person in iʿtikāf perform salat (prayer) in Makkah and outside it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning iʿtikāf and the place of salat (prayer) during it. It distinguishes Makkah from other places, allowing broader prayer space there, while restricting the person in iʿtikāf elsewhere to the specific mosque associated with their retreat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2093 - In a narration from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdullah (as), it is reported:
"The one performing i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in any of its houses as they wish. However, the one performing i'tikaf elsewhere must pray only in the specific mosque designated for their i'tikaf."
